Hold ⌥⌘, ask out loud, and it answers, points at what you need, guides you step by step or drafts the text. It does not send emails, click buttons or log calls for you, so the outreach stays yours.

blocks.text: Where an SDR's day actually goes

If your inbox feels bigger than your phone list, the data backs you up. The Bridge Group's 2025 SDR survey, published in February 2025, covers 351 B2B companies. Its median is 112 activities a day. Of those, 44 are phone calls, 41 are emails, 19 are LinkedIn touches and 8 are texts or other activity.

Activity is not the same as conversation. Phone-first teams in that survey average 56 dials and 4.6 quality conversations a day. Email-first teams average 28 dials and 3.4 quality conversations. The median across all teams is 4.1. The sample leans toward companies with engaged sales development leaders, so your team may look different.

The chart shows the shape of the day. Phone and email make up most of the 112. A dial or an email is only the start, though. Each touch needs research, a note and a follow-up, and that work does not show up in the activity count.
Non-selling work fills most of the day

Broader sales research points the same way. A third-party summary of Salesforce's 2026 State of Sales puts active selling at about 40% of rep time. The other 60% goes to activity logging, manual forecasting, collateral search, pipeline reviews and copying data between systems. The summary gives no separate figure for each task, so read the split as rough.

An older study shows the same pattern. Docurated's State of Sales Productivity 2015, as cited by HubSpot, found that only one-third of a rep's day is spent selling. Reps spent 31% of their time searching for or creating content. Another 20% went to reporting, admin and CRM tasks. The article does not state its sample size, and the data is more than a decade old.
What an AI assistant for SDRs can do on Mac

An AI assistant for SDRs should help with the work between calls and sends, not replace the calls. Lazur covers seven kinds of help. Each one maps to a capability you ask for by voice, or by holding a key.

items: Explain: ask what a field or button does, and Lazur answers out loud from what it can see.
Point: ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen.
Guide: ask how to do a task, and Lazur walks you through it one click at a time, waiting for each click.
Dictate: hold fn and talk. Clean, formatted text lands at the cursor in any app.
Draft: ask for a follow-up or a subject line, and Lazur types the text for you to review.
Research: Lazur runs the job in its own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension, then returns a summary and a report.
Everyday: timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music, opening apps and links, web search and Shortcuts.

blocks.text: Notice what is missing. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. Your CRM, inbox and sheets stay under your control.

Use the question key when you want an answer. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Use the dictation key when you want words typed. Hold fn, talk, and the text lands at your cursor.
A realistic SDR day with Lazur

Here is one plausible Tuesday. The times are examples, not a fixed plan. Each request in the day plan says what you ask and what Lazur does with it. Lazur helps at the moment you ask and never sends for you.

Mornings suit research and calendar checks, when you need facts before the first call. Mid-morning suits dictation, while the call is still fresh. Afternoons suit drafts, because you can read a draft with a clear head.
Gmail sending limits for SDR outbound

Gmail limits shape how you batch outbound, even if one SDR rarely hits them. These figures come from Google's Workspace admin help. They apply to Workspace accounts. A personal Gmail account can have different limits, so check with your admin.

rows: Recipients per message (To, Cc and Bcc)
blocks.caption: Gmail sending limits for Google Workspace, per Google's admin help page.

blocks.text: Counting works differently from what most reps expect. Gmail counts total recipients for each send. Five messages to 10 addresses count as 50. Unique recipients count each address once per day, so five emails to the same 10 people count as 10 unique recipients.

Here is what that means for a normal week. The median SDR sends 41 emails a day, far below a cap of 2,000 messages. The daily cap rarely stops one rep. A long list sent in one batch can run into the per-message and external recipient caps, so split big lists into smaller groups. Limits use a rolling 24-hour window and can change without notice. Google last updated the page on 2026-10-26.
Outlook for Mac and Apple Mail shortcuts

If your team uses Outlook for Mac, check your build before you plan around a feature. Microsoft's release notes list version 16.114.3, released October 27, 2026, with quality and performance fixes only. Version 16.111, from July 14, 2026, lets you edit a message in the Outbox before it sends. That helps when a sequence email goes out with a typo.

Version 16.113, from September 16, 2026, added a remove button for recipients while you compose. It also lets you right-click Mail, Calendar or People in the left rail to open it in a separate window.

Apple Mail has a short set of shortcuts. ⌘N starts a new message, ⌘R replies to the selected email, and ⌃⌘A archives. Apple says shortcuts can vary by language and keyboard layout. If a key does nothing, check the menu, which shows the right shortcut.
Keeping prospect data safe with an AI assistant

Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. When you ask, the audio and a screenshot go to AI providers to get an answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Those are the product's stated terms, so read them before you rely on them for prospect data.

Your employer's rules come first. Many teams set policies for prospect data, customer records and outbound email. Ask your manager or IT team whether screenshots of prospect records can leave your Mac. This page does not make Lazur compliant with any policy or law.
Mistakes SDRs make with an AI assistant

items: Sending a draft unread. Lazur types the text, but you own the send. Read every line for the prospect's name, company and claims.
Trusting research without a check. A background report is a starting point. Open the source before you quote a figure on a call.
Dictating into the wrong field. Dictation lands at the cursor. Click the right box first and look before you speak.
Asking it to do the clicks. Lazur guides you through steps. Ask for the steps, then do them yourself.
Working with no time limit. Inbox sweeps run long when nothing stops them. Start a timer and stop when it rings, even if the inbox is not empty.

blocks.text: What to do next

Pick one task from your day and test it for a week. Good first tests are call notes with dictation, one research job before a call, and a draft you would have written anyway. Track how long each takes, then keep the parts that save time.

For sheet work, read about [sorting data by column](/how-to/sort-data-by-column-in-google-sheets) and [making a dropdown list](/how-to/create-a-dropdown-list-in-google-sheets). For inbox work, read [scheduling an email in Gmail](/how-to/schedule-an-email-to-send-later-in-gmail). When you are ready, compare plans on the [pricing page](/pricing) or [download Lazur](/download).
If your next role shifts toward closing deals, see the [account executive page](/for/account-executives) for that side of the work.

faq.question: Does Lazur send emails or update my CRM for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you. It points at the button, guides you one click at a time, dictates notes at the cursor or types a draft. You review the text and do the send or the save yourself.

faq.question: Is Lazur an add-in for Gmail, Slack or my CRM?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app, and it has no partnership with any app maker. It works with whatever is on your screen while you hold the shortcut.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: What happens to prospect names and screenshots?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Your company's policy still decides what you may share.

faq.question: How does background research work?
faq.answer: You ask for a research job, and it runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Open the sources before you quote a figure on a call.

faq.question: How many emails can one SDR send in Gmail each day?
faq.answer: Google Workspace allows 2,000 messages per user per day, and mail merge is capped at 1,500. Limits use a rolling 24-hour window and can change. Personal Gmail accounts may differ, so ask your admin.

faq.question: Is dictation extra on top of the plan?
faq.answer: Dictation is unlimited on both the Pro and Power plans. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Compare plans on the pricing page.

faq.question: Will an AI assistant replace my CRM or sequence tool?
faq.answer: No. It helps you use the tools you already have. Lazur guides steps, dictates notes and drafts text. Your records stay in the systems your company chose.

painPoints.title: Activity fills the day
painPoints.text: The median SDR logs 112 activities a day. The median number of quality conversations is 4.1. Most of the day never reaches a real talk.

painPoints.title: Email takes the morning
painPoints.text: The median SDR sends 41 emails a day. Each one needs a relevant opening line, a look at the account and a follow-up plan.

painPoints.title: Hunting for content
painPoints.text: Docurated's 2015 data, cited by HubSpot, puts 31% of rep time into searching for or creating content. Most of that search is for the deck or case study you cannot find.

painPoints.title: CRM and reporting admin
painPoints.text: Activity logging, manual forecasting and copying data between systems make up the non-selling work. A third-party summary of Salesforce's 2026 report puts that at about 60% of rep time.

painPoints.title: Dials that do not connect
painPoints.text: Phone-first teams average 56 dials and 4.6 quality conversations a day. Most of the work sits between the dials and the few real talks.

painPoints.title: Sending caps and batching
painPoints.text: Gmail limits for Workspace are high for one rep. Per-message and external recipient caps still shape how you batch a big list.
